text:
ashley: Heads-up — noticed a p99 tail-latency bump on prod for 8k sequences after the kernel-selector change yesterday. Not across the board, only a subset of pods in us-west2. :thinking_face:

leo: How big are the formed batches when you see the spike? small batches + flash path could be bad for KV churn.

ashley: Batches are often 2-6 requests (typical token budgets ~1200-2500 per request). We usually see steady throughput but these pods show a higher fraction of tiny microbatches. grabbed a quick flame output:```
# quick flame (30s)
kernel_select: flash_attn 68%
paged_kv_handler: 18%
fallback_attn: 14%
KV_miss: 11% of requests (spiky)
avg_batch_size: 3.4
```

mike: @ashley thanks — did the kernel-selector recently start preferring flash for small sequence lengths? I thought we gated flash when avg_batch_size < 4.

ashley: That was the intent. The new heuristic uses a moving-average sequence-length *and* a per-queue token-budget override. I think the token-budget cap is being hit, causing queue slicing so we end up with more small batches but flash still gets chosen because seq_len estimator is slightly optimistic.

sylvia: Can you dump the queue policy for the affected pod? Also, which commit rolled the selector?

ashley: Pod config snippet: ```
batcher.window_ms: 12
batcher.token_budget_target: 16384
queue.max_hold_ms: 40
kernel_selector.enable_flash_threshold: 0.6
kernel_selector.seq_len_smooth_alpha: 0.12
```
Commit: 3b9f7a4 — "kernel: prefer flash when seq_est >= 0.6"

leo: If token_budget_target is 16384 and most requests are long-ish, the batcher may slice into narrow groups to respect per-request token caps. That + smoother alpha means seq_est lags real-time. Flash gives better throughput for big seqs but worse constant factors for tiny batches (ram/dma overhead).

perf-bot: Automated profiler note — detected increased kernel_switch_count on node i-0a1b2c (recent selector commit present).

mike: Hypothesis: when queue forms small batches, flash kernel introduces page faults in paged-KV path because the KV prefetcher expects larger coalesced access. This spikes p99 for individual requests. Two experiments to try: 1) tighten flash threshold to 0.8 (avoid flash for marginal seq estimates), 2) increase batcher.window_ms to 20 to give more time for batching.

ashley: Agreed. I can canary both on a subset of pods. Which do you want first?

mike: Start with gating flash (threshold 0.8) on 10% of traffic, run for 30m. If p99 improves, follow with increasing window on next 10%.

sylvia: Also monitor paged-KV eviction rate and GPU memcpy stalls. Add these to the canary dashboard. I recommend adding a perf regression alert: if kernel_switch_count increases >20% or KV_miss_rate > 5% spike, auto-roll metrics notify.

ashley: Will deploy canary now. config diff: ```diff
- kernel_selector.enable_flash_threshold: 0.6
+ kernel_selector.enable_flash_threshold: 0.8  # canary 10%
- batcher.window_ms: 12
+ batcher.window_ms: 12
```

leo: One more idea — try small-batch fusion: if avg_batch_size < 4, prefer the fallback kernel that has optimized small-seq path (lower per-batch overhead). We could add that as a short-term workaround.

mike: Yes, but that becomes a two-axis policy (seq_len + batch_size). Might be simpler to bias selector by expected_batch_cost = f(seq_len, expected_batch_size). We should capture expected_batch_size in the selector state.

ashley: Canary rollout started at 1979998920. Perf bot will log results.

perf-bot: Canary update @1979998975 — p99 reduced by ~18% on canary pods, KV_miss_rate down 9% relative to baseline. No errors observed.

ashley: Nice. I'll keep canary running for 1h and then try increasing window_ms on another 10%. If that also helps, we can combine both changes in the selector logic.

sylvia: Please open a follow-up RFC in eng-runtime for making selector consider expected batch size and add unit tests around the paging behavior. Also add a small perf test that simulates tiny microbatch workloads (random short/long mix).

mike: Filed PERF-3125 with notes and repro harness link: https://bugs/repro/PERF-3125 — include the flame and canary graphs.

ashley: Thanks all. I'll post final canary summary after 1h. :thumbsup:

leo: Thanks — good catch.
